summary: William Edelglass works in philosophy and Buddhist studies. He taught philosophy at Colby College (attested 2007) and held posts as Professor at Marlboro College (attested 2013) and Visiting Professor at the Institute of Buddhist Dialectics.

William Edward Soothill, a scholar of Sinology and Buddhist studies, studied at the University of London. He served as Director of Shanxi University (1907-1911), was at National Central University (1911), and was Professor of Chinese at Oxford (1920-1935).

William Erskine worked in Indology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and history and archaeology. Educated at the Royal High School and the University of Edinburgh (~1787-1792), he founded the Asiatic Society of Mumbai (1804) and served the Literary Society of Bombay (~1804-1823).
William Evans Hoyle studied at Owens College from around 1872 to 1874 and at Christ Church, Oxford, from around 1874 to 1877.

William F. Powell is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Sinology, and religious studies. Attested at the University of California, Santa Barbara from 1986, he is attested there in 2026 as Emeritus Professor of Religious Studies and Research Professor.

William Fairfield Warren studied at Wesleyan, Andover Theological Seminary, and Mystical Seven. Working in religious studies and philosophy, he taught at the Methodist Episcopal Missionary Institute (1860-1866) and served as Boston University's first President and Professor (1873-1911).

William Foster, an Indologist and historian, earned a B.A. at the University of London. He worked at the India Office from 1882, notably as Registrar and Superintendent of Records (1907-1927), and served as President of the Hakluyt Society (1928-1945).

William Foxwell Albright studied at Upper Iowa University (~1907-1912) and Johns Hopkins University (~1913-1916). A scholar of history, linguistics, and religious studies, he was Acting Director of ASOR (1921-1922) and Professor of Semitic Languages at Johns Hopkins (1929-1958).
William Francklin, who worked in history, archaeology, and Indology, was educated at Westminster School and studied at Trinity College, Cambridge, from around 1781 to 1782.

William Frederic Sinclair, who worked in history, archaeology, and Indology, was educated at Royal School, Armagh. He joined the Indian Civil Service in 1866 and held administrative positions in the Bombay Presidency from around 1871 to 1897.

William Frederick Travers O'Connor, a Tibetologist, studied at Charterhouse School (1884-1887) and the Royal Military Academy, Woolwich (~1888-1890). He received a post in the Royal Artillery in 1890.

William Frederick Webster was an Indologist educated at the City of London School, Trinity College, Cambridge (1874), and Lincoln's Inn (1879). At Cambridge, he studied under Edward Byles Cowell in 1874.

William G. Archer, a scholar of Indology, history, and archaeology, studied at the University of Cambridge (~1928-1931) and SOAS University of London. He served as Keeper of the Indian Section at the Victoria and Albert Museum (1949-1959).

William George Grey was an Indologist and linguist who received an honorary M.A. from the University of Cambridge in 1931. He served as Lecturer in Urdu at Gonville and Caius College from 1929 to 1940.

Sinologist William H. Nienhauser, Jr. studied at Indiana University under Irving Yucheng Lo and Friedrich Alexander Bischoff, as well as at Bonn. He served as Professor and Halls-Bascom Professor of Classical Chinese Literature at the University of Wisconsin-Madison from 1983.

William H. Wiser, active in Indology, studied at the University of Chicago (B.A.) and Cornell University (Ph.D.). He held posts at Sam Higginbottom University (1915) and as Professor of Rural Sociology at North India Theological College (1933-1941).

William Harlen Gilbert, Jr. earned his Ph.D. at the University of Chicago (~1930-1935). Active in Indology, he taught sociology at Auburn University (1936-1937) and served at the Library of Congress from around 1941 to 1972.

William Harrison Moreland was a scholar of Indology, history, and archaeology. Educated at Clifton College and Trinity College, Cambridge (~1886-1889), he served in the Indian Civil Service from around 1889 to 1914.
William Hay Macnaghten, who worked in Indology, was educated at Charterhouse School and later studied at Fort William College in 1816.
William Henry Carmichael Smyth, a scholar of linguistics and Indology, was educated at Charterhouse School. He served as Resident Superintendent at Addiscombe Military Seminary from 1822 to 1824.
